newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair plans Lottery-funded arts "bank".
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair plans Lottery-funded arts "bank".

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair on Monday proposed setting up a Lottery-funded trust to launch the artists of tomorrow.
The National Endowment for Science and the Arts (NESTA) could raise up to 100 million pounds and end up being self-financed from copyright and royalty payments.
"NESTA would be a 21st century National Trust for Talent in Britain, backing human capital rather than buildings," the Labour leader told senior television and film executives.
Cash from the hugely successful National Lottery has in the past been channelled into capital projects like new buildings.
"The Endowment would be launched with tranches of lottery funds after the Millenium and be built up with gifts or assignments of copyright and patent royalties," he said.
Blair, opinion poll favourite to win the next election due by May, promised to nurture talent in the British film industry, so often heralded for revivals that never quite materialise.

"I sometimes feel British cinema is a bit like one of those Dracula movies -- just when you think it is dead and buried, it springs back to life with renewed vigour. We are on an upswing at the moment, which is good, but we must sustain it," he said.

Blair, making his first major policy speech on the arts, applauded British talent for winning 30 percent of all the Hollywood Oscars in the past 20 years. He said British recording artists capture 20 percent of world sales.
Britain's arts are a 10 billion pound ($16 billion) export industry which employs about 750,000 people and is the overriding attraction for tourists visiting Britain, he said.
With both parties eager to score pre-election points off each other, National Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley was quick to condemn Blair's proposal.
"This luvvies' charter confirms my worst fears. This Labour scheme for a politically correct Lottery will be at the expense of communities up and down the country," she said.
"Luvvies" is the nickname for actors and film stars, many of whom publicly support Labour and have openly attacked the ruling Conservatives for their disinterest in the arts.
